verification.note: Unit 12 (Polymers), printed as VSAQ 21 on book p.97. The 1+1 mark split is a CLAIM, not the board scheme, until a Telangana IPE teacher confirms it; the question itself is sourced, not invented. Source: the chemistry half of "FAST TRACK IPE for Sr. Students", printed chapter 9 (POLYMERS), book pp.95-98 (PDF pp.34-37), which is unit 12 in this bank. The chapter is VSAQ-only: it prints 24 Very Short Answer Questions and has no Short Answer and no Long Answer section at all, and no PROBLEMS. Neither the two-book union check nor a board back-test was possible for Chemistry-II: the TSBIE Basic Learning Material on hand is physics-only and first-year, and no second-year chemistry paper is in the corpus. BOOK: the printed answer is "Polymers which are formed from more than one kind of monomer units are called copolymers", with examples "Nylon-6, 6, terylene". Both are correct and are kept. The monomers are supplied. ADDED: the point that a copolymer may be either an addition or a condensation polymer, because both printed examples are condensation polymers and a student who sees only those may conclude that all copolymers are.

page_header: Section A — Very Short Answer Question

steps.label: The definition
lines: A copolymer is a polymer made from more
Units of both monomers appear in the same
chain, either in a regular alternating
A copolymer may be an addition polymer or
a condensation polymer; only the number
steps.why: The definition turns on monomer types alone, so a two monomer addition polymer such as Buna-S and a two monomer condensation polymer such as nylon-6,6 are both copolymers. Adding a second monomer is how a chemist changes one property without rebuilding the whole chain.
common_mistakes: Writing that a copolymer must have two different functional groups. It must have two different MONOMERS.
Writing that a copolymer is a mixture of two polymers. The two units sit in the same chain.
steps.memory_tip: Co means together: two monomers together in one chain.
steps.margin_note: The words more than one kind of monomer are the mark.

steps.label: Examples with their monomers
lines: copolymers; Buna-S is an addition one.
steps.why: The three examples cover both routes to a copolymer, so one of them fits whatever the examiner asks next. Writing the two monomers beside each name is what shows the definition was applied and not recited.
common_mistakes: Giving polythene or PVC. Each has one monomer, so each is a homopolymer.
Naming terylene with only one monomer. It needs both ethylene glycol and terephthalic acid.
steps.memory_tip: Every polymer in this chapter with two monomer names after it is a copolymer.
steps.margin_note: Two examples with their monomers finish this mark.

insider_note: Copolymer and homopolymer are asked as a pair in this chapter. Define both by counting monomer types, never by counting functional groups.
